transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood, AE); Mateo Ruiz (Redwood, SE); Dana Chen (Citrine, Head of Security); Arjun Mehta (Citrine, CTO); Lena Ortiz (Compliance Manager); Nora Blake (Legal)

Summary:
High-level security review focused on key management (BYOK/HSM), data residency in EU/US, audit log retention, RBAC/SSO integration, and explicit confirmation of 'no training on customer data' and prompt retention policies. Customer provided their regulatory scope (EU data residency + some US operations with PHI handling), asked for technical controls, evidence of SOC 2/ISO, and options for private deployment vs hosted with VPC.

Topics covered:
- SOC 2 and ISO status and evidence
- KMS options: Redwood-managed vs BYOK with HSM
- Data residency and region pinning
- Audit logs, retention and export format
- RBAC, SSO (SAML/Okta) and session traceability
- Data handling: prompt retention, PII/PHI policy, no-train guarantees, ephemerality options

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: All right everyone thanks for joining, um we can start — I'm Jamie from Redwood, AE. I'll hand over to Mateo, our solutions engineer, who will drive the technical Qs, but wanted to set context: this call is to validate infosec requirements and talk KMS etc.
[00:18] Mateo Ruiz: Hi all, yea thanks. Quick round robin? maybe two minutes each.
[00:23] Dana Chen: Dana here, head of security at Citrine. We look after infosec and data governance. Primary questions are KMS, no-training on customer data, and data residency.
[00:33] Arjun Mehta: Arjun, CTO. We'll be using the API for clinical routing workflows and some models will see PHI in the prompts, so encryption + audit trail are critical.
[00:44] Lena Ortiz: Lena, compliance. SOC 2 and ISO artifacts required for procurement. Also retention windows for logs.
[00:50] Nora Blake: Nora, legal — short on time but want confirmation that Redwood cannot use our prompts to train models and scope of indemnities.
[00:58] Mateo Ruiz: Great, thanks. Jumping into KMS first. At a high level Redwood supports both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (BYOK). For BYOK we integrate with cloud KMS providers and can also do HSM-backed keys, and customers can rotate keys. Is that the direction you're thinking?
[01:15] Dana Chen: We prefer BYOK with HSM, conceptually, because of our compliance program. Can you clarify the HSM provenance — AWS CloudHSM vs on-prem HSM?
[01:26] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, we commonly support AWS KMS with CloudHSM backing or Azure Key Vault HSM. For Private deployments we can integrate with a customer HSM using a PKCS#11 bridge. For hosted customers, BYOK means you import a key or do an external key wrapping workflow; Redwood never stores the unwrapped raw key. There was a question earlier about ephemeral session keys — we use envelope encryption.
[01:51] Dana Chen: envelope encryption plus HSM wrapping, good. And logs — are key usage and crypto ops surfaced in audit logs?
[01:59] Mateo Ruiz: Key ops are logged. Audit trail includes key usage events, request IDs, caller identity. We can export logs in JSON and ship to a customer S3 or SIEM via secure webhook. Retention configurable on Dedicated/Private. Hosted default is 90 days but we can extend for enterprise.
[02:18] Lena Ortiz: Quick Q on SOC 2 — do you have a Type II report, and does it cover private deployments?
[02:25] Jamie Park: We have a SOC 2 Type II for our hosted service. Private deployments are covered via enterprise agreement but we also provide architecture docs and customer-specific attestations. I'll share the SOC2 report after the call.
[02:37] Nora Blake: And ISO 27001 — do you have cert or in process?
[02:41] Jamie Park: We're ISO 27001 certified as of late 2025, so yes we can provide that cert and scope.
[02:48] Arjun Mehta: Good. On data residency — we need EU-only processing for patient data. Can you guarantee that for hosted?
[02:57] Mateo Ruiz: We do region pinning. For hosted API, you can choose region (EU-west or US-east, for example). Requests sent to EU region remain in EU processing, and logs can be stored in region. For stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control the VPC and storage account.
[03:16] Dana Chen: How do you prevent accidental routing to other regions during failover? We need SLOs but not if it means data egress to non-EU.
[03:26] Mateo Ruiz: Good point. We have routing policies — you can set strict region affinity so fallback will not cross residency boundaries. The default autoscale fallback may cross regions, but we can configure per-customer policies to block cross-border fallback.
[03:44] Lena Ortiz: Audit log retention — default 90 days, you said. For procurement we need 1 year of immutable logs. Is that possible?
[03:52] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we support 1+ year retention and write-once storage options; hosted can be extended via add-on. We also provide tamper-evident log digests (hash chains) on request.
[04:08] Dana Chen: Now, the big one — training on customer data. We need a hard, contractually backed NO-TRAIN statement with technical controls. Can you describe how Redwood enforces no-training?
[04:21] Jamie Park: Short answer: we do not use customer data to continue training or to update model weights. We offer a model that is static for inference and we disable any logging or data capture that would feed into model-training pipelines. Mateos, do you want to go into the technical?
[04:35] Mateo Ruiz: Sure. Our production infra separates inference telemetry from training platforms. The training pipeline is a separate cluster with explicit ingestion jobs and access controls. Customer request/response data by default is not routed to training storage. We have an internal 'no-train' flag that, when set at the tenant level, prevents any downstream export to training buckets. We also redact or hash PII fields if configured. The model instances do not persist new weights in production.
[05:02] Nora Blake: Is the 'no-train' flag auditable? We need evidence for contracts.
[05:08] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, setting changes are recorded in the audit log with user and timestamp. We can show configuration snapshots and the audit log of that tenant.
[05:15] Dana Chen: What about prompt retention — do you keep raw prompts? How long? Are they accessible to humans?
[05:22] Mateo Ruiz: By default hosted keeps request/response for 30 days for debugging. They are accessible to engineers for debugging under RBAC and only after approval; we can enable ephemerality which removes storage immediately after inference or configure shorter windows. For POC we can enable ephemerality + no-human-access. For enterprise we can set a 0-day retention and rely on logs only.
[05:46] Arjun Mehta: We must avoid humans seeing PHI. Can you guarantee that human reviewers will not access prompts?
[05:53] Mateo Ruiz: We have a human access policy. Human review is very limited and only occurs when an automated system flags an anomaly, and it requires a documented approval workflow. For PHI customers we can disable human review entirely and require Private deployment if you want no possibility of human access.
[06:10] Dana Chen: Encryption of data in transit and at rest? And are logs encrypted with separate keys?
[06:16] Mateo Ruiz: TLS 1.2+ in transit; at rest we use envelope encryption: data keys per-tenant encrypted by the KMS root. Audit logs are encrypted with a separate key namespace and can be managed by the customer's BYOK.
[06:28] Lena Ortiz: RBAC and SSO — we use Okta for SAML. How does Redwood integrate?
[06:34] Jamie Park: We support SAML SSO and OIDC, with SCIM for user provisioning. Roles map to RBAC policies in the console. You can create least-privilege roles and restrict access to logs and dev tools.
[06:47] Nora Blake: For legal, what is your default data processor/ controller stance and can we get a DPA with no-training clause?
[06:53] Jamie Park: We are flexible — our standard DPA includes a no-training clause for enterprise. We can include audit rights and data residency commitments in the SOW.
[07:03] Arjun Mehta: One more - exportability of logs and ability to run our own integrity checks?
[07:09] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, you can pull raw JSON log exports and we also support streaming to your SIEM. You can run hash checks on the digests we provide.
[07:20] Dana Chen: On-boarding controls — for POC we want to push some sample PHI-like payloads. What's the recommended posture?
[07:28] Mateo Ruiz: For initial testing we suggest Private deployment in your VPC or host a Dedicated node in EU region and enable BYOK + ephemerality. If you must use hosted, enable ephemerality and no-human-access and restrict region to EU. We'll also bind the 'no-train' flag.
[07:46] Lena Ortiz: Regarding certifications — can you provide evidence of penetration test and the scope?
[07:51] Jamie Park: Yes, we do annual pentests and can share executive summaries and remediations. The full report is under NDA; we can facilitate that exchange.
[07:59] Nora Blake: Any third-party sub-processors we should be worried about?
[08:04] Mateo Ruiz: We publish a sub-processor list. Core infra is run on AWS; we might use GCP or Azure in some regions. For EU-only customers we can restrict to particular cloud providers and document the boundaries.
[08:18] Dana Chen: Can you walk through an example audit log event for a prompt? I'd like to see fields.
[08:24] Mateo Ruiz: Sure. Example fields: timestamp, request_id, tenant_id, model_version, region, input_hash (sha256), user_id, API_key_id, action, result_status. We don't log raw input by default unless retention is enabled. If you need raw output for debugging it's stored encrypted and the key usage is logged.
[08:47] Arjun Mehta: What about model explainability — we need to tie outputs to model version and deterministic seeds for reproducibility.
[08:55] Mateo Ruiz: We include model_version and inference container metadata in the log. We also can record RNG seeds and KV cache sizes on request to reproduce behaviors.
[09:06] Dana Chen: On indemnities — standard SaaS indemnities ok but need contractual no-training plus audit rights.
[09:12] Nora Blake: Yes, and breach notification SLA.
[09:15] Jamie Park: That's all negotiable; we typically agree to 72-hour breach notification and include contractual no-train. We'll flag legal to draft with your counsel.
[09:24] Dana Chen: If the no-train flag is accidentally turned off, what controls prevent data from leaking into training?
[09:31] Mateo Ruiz: Several controls: 1) separation of train infra, 2) role-based gating around ingestion jobs, 3) processing pipelines require explicit, logged approvals, and 4) we have n-day buffer checks with manual review for any dataset promoted to training. The promotion process is auditable.
[09:52] Lena Ortiz: For procurement, how quickly can you provide required docs? SOC2 and pentest summaries we need within a week ideally.
[09:59] Jamie Park: We can provide SOC2 and pentest summaries this week — I'll send by Friday.
[10:05] Dana Chen: Re: data erasure — if we terminate, can you purge all our data including backups?
[10:12] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, data deletion options include immediate purge and certified deletion. Backup purge windows vary; for hosted we can remove within 30 days of request; for Dedicated/Private we can purge immediately if you have the right contract terms. We'll produce a deletion certificate.
[10:28] Arjun Mehta: Do you support field-level redaction or inline PII masking?
[10:33] Mateo Ruiz: We support pre-ingest redaction plugins and on-the-fly masking rules. You can also run a DLP engine pre-call to strip sensitive fields.
[10:41] Dana Chen: One operational question — who manages the SRE runbooks for fallback and are they accessible? We need to map incident response with our own SOC.
[10:50] Jamie Park: We have runbooks and SOC playbooks; we can share redacted runbooks under NDA and align on joint incident response for Dedicated/Private. For hosted, we include an incident playbook and support SLA.
[11:05] Nora Blake: Can we add a clause preventing future changes to default retention without notice?
[11:10] Jamie Park: Yes, we can include change control and notice periods in the contract.
[11:15] Dana Chen: Okay, let's recap next steps.
[11:18] Jamie Park: Recap: We'll send SOC2 and ISO certs + pentest executive summary; Mateo will send KMS/BYOK integration doc and an architecture diagram showing private deployment in EU with HSM; we'll propose a 30-day POC in EU with ephemerality, BYOK and no-human-access; legal teams to discuss DPA with no-train clause and breach notification SLA.
[11:41] Arjun Mehta: Sounds good. Can we get a timeline for the POC resources?
[11:46] Mateo Ruiz: We can spin a dedicated pilot in 5 business days once the contract and SSO are agreed.
[11:52] Dana Chen: Perfect. Thank you.
[11:55] Jamie Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with artifacts and schedule.
[11:59] Meeting end.
